definition: קָאַת , קָאָת noun [feminine] a bird, usually pelican (compare ᵐ5 Leviticus, Deuteronomy, Psalms, ᵑ9 Psalms (derived by Thes from [ קוא ], קיא (see Kö ii. 1, 173 , and, on ת , Ges «GKC:80g»§ 80g ), as throwing up food from its crop for its young); but sea-fowl improbable in Psalms, Isaiah; Late Hebrew קָאָת , ᵑ7 קָאתָא id. ); — absolute הַקָּאָת Lev 11:18 = Deut 14:17 , as unclean; קָאַת ( van d. H. Gi ; Baer קָאָת ) Isa 34:11 ; Zeph 2:14 , as inhabiting ruins; construct קְאַת מִדְכָּר Ps 102:7 , simile of loneliness. קַב see I. קבב . Below
